sentences.text: Donald Burgess, who had dementia, was pepper sprayed and Tasered in his wheelchair Two police officers who pepper-sprayed and Tasered a 92-year-old amputee at a care home have been sacked for gross misconduct.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: PC Stephen Smith and PC Rachel Comotto, who were both acquitted of assault occasioning actual bodily harm in May 2025, had been called to Park Beck care home in St Leonards-on-Sea after resident Donald Burgess threatened carers with a dinner knife.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Burgess, who had dementia, was hit with a baton, pepper sprayed and Tasered as he sat in his wheelchair in his bedroom in June 2022.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: At Sussex Police headquarters in Lewes earlier, a disciplinary panel decided there had been "unjustified and excessive use of force" and dismissed both officers without notice.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Burgess was taken to hospital after the incident, where he contracted Covid and died 22 days later, but the officers were not held responsible for his death.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: The misconduct panel found Comotto and Smith did not attempt to de-escalate the situation before using force and had breached standards of professional behaviour.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Both have been placed on the College of Policing's barred list.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: PC Rachel Comotto and PC Stephen Smith were dismissed from the force without notice During a week-long hearing, force lawyer Aaron Rathmell told the panel Smith, 52, and Comotto, 37, "acted, hastily, harshly and lost control".
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: He said Smith had drawn the pepper spray within nine seconds of entering Burgess's room.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Bodyworn camera footage showed Smith walking into the room and saying: "Do you want to be sprayed or Tasered?
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Can you put that down for us?" Despite repeated requests, Burgess, who was a single leg amputee, did not drop the dinner knife.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: The panel found Smith "made no attempt to assess or understand" Burgess' vulnerability, while Comotto "showed no compassion".
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: The following video contains distressing scenes.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: This video can not be played Body-worn camera footage shows Burgess being asked to put down the knife Smith failed to consider leaving the 92-year-old in his room to calm down, the panel found, plus the use of Pava, a type of pepper spray, was deemed unreasonable in the circumstances.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: There was "limited mitigation" for this behaviour, it said.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: The panel also said Smith's tone and language towards Burgess was "dismissive in nature", while Comotto was "antagonistic".
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Comotto's statements - such as "last chance" or "seriously" - and giving Burgess limited time to respond, were found to be inappropriate.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: The panel found her use of force to be unreasonable.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Assistant Chief Constable Peter Gardner said Burgess was in his own room, isolated from residents and posed no risk.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: More information should have been ascertained from care home staff, he said.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Gardner added that Smith had shown a lack of remorse and insight into the inappropriateness of his actions, and the panel remained concerned by his evidence which stated he would not do anything differently.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: While noting Comotto's remorse and evidence that she would act differently, Gardner said the reputation of the police service, along with public confidence in it, must be upheld.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: Deputy Chief Constable Paul Court said Smith and Comotto's conduct "in no way reflects" that of others in the force After the hearing, Deputy Chief Constable Paul Court said he was "appalled" by the officers' actions and apologised to the Burgess family.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: He said Smith and Comotto's behaviour "in no way reflects the conduct of those who serve in Sussex Police, particularly when responding to incidents involving vulnerable people and those in crisis".
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: He said police officers "can often find themselves in challenging and unpredictable situations, where they must make split-second decisions to keep the public safe and to do so with measure, compassion and skill.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: "This was not one of those cases." Speaking after the hearing, Burgess' great nephew, Jason Pye, called him "a much loved family man" who should be "remembered for the life he lived and not simply for the events which brought us to this point".
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: He said justice had been served and dismissal from Sussex Police was "the only outcome there could have been" for Smith and Comotto.
sentences.article_title: PCs who used Taser and baton on amputee, 92, sacked

sentences.text: He added: "I hope this is a warning to all officers who show that sort of behaviour going forward." Follow BBC Sussex on Facebook , external , on X , external , and on Instagram , external and listen to BBC Radio Sussex on Sounds .

sentences.article_title: UK special forces could face prosecution as Afghanistan evidence referred to police

sentences.text: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) found the evidence earlier this year, following investigation by the SAS Inquiry, and then UKSF referred it to the military police's Defence Serious Crime Unit (DSCU), a specialist unit set up in 2022 to deal with the most serious crimes.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Amanda Mathewson leaves Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court A Dunfermline childminder has admitted leaving more than 20 children she was caring for alone and unsupervised in her home.

sentences.text: Amanda Mathewson, 55, pleaded guilty at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court to neglect and abandoning children in her care.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Her offending took place at a number of locations in Dunfermline and elsewhere in Fife.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The court heard Mathewson had 27 children in her home, 19 more than she was licensed to look after.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Mathewson, who has been a self-employed childminder for 30 years, was arrested by police following allegations of cruelty towards children.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The court heard she had provided childcare services at her home in Dunfermline for children under the age of 16.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: At the time of her arrest she had 15 children aged under 12, 10 children under primary school age, and two children under the age of one in her care.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: More stories from Edinburgh, Fife & East More stories from Scotland Procurator fiscal Vicki Bell told the court two parents became suspicious of Mathewson after being informed their children were not present while the childminder carried out a school run.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: They secretly went to the school and found their children were not with Mathewson, despite being in her care.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: They then went to her home, where they heard a "child screaming" and found five unattended children in the garden.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: One of the children told the witnesses there were no adults inside, and Mathewson had told them to "wait in the garden".
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: They approached the door of the house to check if there were any adults present, when they hear another child "screaming hysterically" inside.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The door was unlocked, and when the witnesses entered they found a child crying under the kitchen table.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: A further nine children, all under five, were found in an upstairs bedroom.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Two of them were strapped into prams.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The children were said to be "distressed" but uninjured.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Police attended and Mathewson said the children had been left alone for at least 30 minutes.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The court heard ring doorbell footage showed it was the second time that day the children had been left inside the house.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: During the police investigation, various children told their parents that being left alone in Mathewson's home was "commonplace".
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Some parents told officers that their children became "upset" when they were taken to the childminder's home and those who could talk would say they did not want to go.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The investigation found discrepancies in the number of children in Matthewson's care and the number of children she was seen with on multiple occasions.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: For example, Mathewson attended a church Christmas party with three children, despite having nine kids in her care that day.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The parents of the three children who were in attendance were sent a photo of their child with Santa, while the others were just sent a generic photo.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: There were other occasions such as a sports day and a visit to Dunfermline fire station where Mathewson was seen with fewer children than she was responsible for.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Parents also raised concerns that their children had not eaten while in the childminder's care due to their clothes staying in "pristine condition" and it was a general theme that their children would return home thirsty.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Some parents also reported their children returned home in dirty nappies or with dry faeces in their underwear.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Court documents state that Mathewson always had loud music playing and did not let parents enter her home at drop off time in an attempt to "conceal how oversubscribed she was".
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: When the childminder was asked about the number of children in her care, or the whereabouts of certain children she claimed she was being assisted by a "child-minding friend".
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The case was heard at at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court Mathewson admitted wilfully neglecting, abandoning and exposing children to a manner likely to cause them unnecessary suffering or injury to their health.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The court heard she offered childcare places for more children than she could reasonably provide care for at the time.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: A Care Inspectorate report published in August 2023 said Mathewson was registered to provide care for a maximum of eight children at any one time.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: It included conditions that a maximum of six children could be under the age of 12, no more than three could have started primary school, and no more than one could be under 12-months-old.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The unannounced inspection from about a year before her arrest had rated areas including care, learning and the setting as "very good", the second-highest level in the quality scale.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: The report said "children were cared for in a comfortable, welcoming and homely environment" and "were cared for with warmth, kindness and a nurturing approach".
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Care Inspectorate said it was a "distressing case" and they had implemented changes as a result.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Police Scotland said it was a "complex investigation" that involved working with a number of partner agencies.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: A force spokesperson said: "We remain wholly committed to supporting victims of crime and protecting children from harm and will use all available resources during our investigation.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: "We urge anyone with concerns about a child protection matter to speak to police , external in the knowledge that you will be fully supported and listened to." In a statement given to the BBC, one of the parents said: "The criminal case is important for justice.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: But our ultimate goal is to ensure no other family has to endure what we have been through.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: Our trust was broken, but our resolve is not.
sentences.article_title: Childminder who left 27 children alone in her home pleads guilty to neglect

sentences.text: "We have turned our pain into a purpose: to rebuild the system of childcare regulation and family support so that it is truly fit to protect Scotland's children." Sheriff John MacRitchie deferred sentencing until 6 November to allow background reports to be carried out.

sentences.text: So what is pneumonic plague, and how dangerous is it?
sentences.article_title: What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread?

sentences.text: Pneumonic plague is a really serious lung infection, often described as the most virulent form of plague.
sentences.article_title: What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread?

sentences.text: There are two other types of plague: bubonic, which affects the lymph nodes; and septicaemic, which affects the blood.
sentences.article_title: What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread?

sentences.text: Pneumonic plague can occur after an initial infection of one of these other types.
sentences.article_title: What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread?

sentences.text: Symptoms include shortness of breath, chest pain, and often coughing up blood.

sentences.text: Paramount Skydance has officially taken over Warner Bros Discovery in a $110bn merger that is set to reshape Hollywood and the media landscape.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: The takeover - merging two of the biggest studios in Los Angeles - comes after months of legal disputes and widespread criticism over feared cuts and consolidation could harm competition and consumers.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: It will alter streaming for millions, usher in a new chapter in the film and TV industry, and leave one of the biggest US news outlets, CNN, in uncertain territory.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: The merger will also bring together a host of entities including HBO, CBS, Nickelodeon, Showtime, Comedy Central, DC Studios and Food Network.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: Paramount will acquire ownership of iconic franchises that include Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, The Lord of the Rings to add to its existing catalogue of hit franchises which includes Indiana Jones, Mission: Impossible and Shrek.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: The newly merged entertainment behemoth will be re-branded under the name Skydance Corporation, the company originally founded by David Ellison before he took over both Paramount and Warner Bros Discover.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: Ellison, chairman and chief executive of Skydance, said the completion of the deal was "historic" for the film industry.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: "From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: Now that ambition is a reality," he said.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: Kreiz will focus on the company's day-to-day operations, including integrating the  newly-combined businesses, while Ellison will focus on strategy and technology.
sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.article_title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger

sentences.text: An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

sentences.text: City have appealed against the verdict.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: However, there is said to be a consensus among a group of top-flight club executives that if City's appeal is unsuccessful, the sanctions should make reparations for the period when they broke the rules, while also limiting their powers in future.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: There is also a feeling from at least four Premier League boardrooms that a "one-hit" points deduction resulting in relegation to the Championship would be an insufficient punishment given the severity of City's wrongdoing.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: There is understood to be nuance in exactly what clubs consider a fitting penalty for the eight-time Premier League champions, who were found guilty of all serious financial rule breaches in a damning verdict by an independent commission.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: One senior club source said City should be stripped of their titles, and added there was "no great rush" among clubs to push for the redistribution of trophies, but rather to take honours away and leave them vacant.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: The source warned the credibility of the Premier League would be lost if City were allowed to keep the eight major trophies they won during the period they have been found guilty.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: However, in a sign of a range of opinions across the league, BBC Sport was previously told there was little appetite among other clubs for City to be stripped of titles.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: Regarding the timescale for sanctions in the future, there is a concern among club executives that a sanction applied just to one season would merely provide City with a "bump in the road" given the likelihood of them returning to the Premier League at the first time of asking.
sentences.article_title: Rival clubs want retrospective and future punishments for Man City

sentences.text: A number of Premier League figures therefore believe any points deduction should be split over multiple seasons, while there is also a sense that transfer bans that stretch over a number of windows would also significantly hinder City's ability to regain their top-flight status as quickly as possible.

sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Anastasiia says she will no longer travel on Ukraine's railways after a drone strike near her train last month For a railway company proud of its record for punctuality, this year's disrupted schedule is posing a major challenge.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "We used to say that that during times of war we performed better than some railways in Europe in regular times,"the head of rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia, Oleksandr Pertsovskyi, told us.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "But now the life of our passengers and crew members is the utmost priority." Russia's defence ministry denies targeting Ukrainian civilians and says its attacks on railways target the infrastructure used to transport military personnel and equipment.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: The dangers are very real.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Attacks on Ukrzaliznytsia's rolling stock and stations have risen sharply.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Of the 521 locomotives hit since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, almost 60% have been this year, according to statistics released by the company.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Overall attacks on railway facilities have risen from 1,206 in 2025 to 1,700 so far this year.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Confronting Russia's threat of Ukraine's railways is a game of cat and mouse, says Oleksandr Pertsovskyi, CEO of Ukrzaliznytsia "The latest wave of escalation and real war with railways is becoming extremely intense," said Pertsovskyi.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "It's a combination of the deadly force of their shahed drones and precision that they achieve with cameras and mesh networks so they can hit moving targets." According to Pertsovskyi, some of Russia's most recent drones are equipped with AI tools and image recognition.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Ukraine is understandably cagey about how it goes about confronting this increasingly sophisticated threat, but electronic methods to disrupt the drones' connectivity are high on the list.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, this is always a cat-and-mouse game," he said.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: On one huge video screen, colour-coded passenger and freight trains could be seen making their way along the arteries of Ukraine's vast railway network.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: We watched as a red icon representing a drone appeared to loiter over Kyiv, practically above our heads at one point.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Each drone had a 100km (62-mile) circle around it.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Any passenger trains inside the circle would already have been evacuated, with customers not allowed to reboard until the train was outside the circle and the drone was still moving away.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "Our mission is not to let our train or our crew members be in that immediate attack area," Pertsovskyi said.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Some train stoppages can last hours, causing chaos for passengers across Ukraine's rail networks The company's precautions appear to have kept casualties low.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Its figures for 2026 show that eight company employees have been killed, six of them when a ballistic missile struck a locomotive depot in Kyiv.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: During our visit to Iron Command, another air raid siren sounded in Kyiv.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: The city's main railway station, we were told, was being evacuated.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: On a later visit to the busy station, we found passengers waiting outside the main entrance or sheltering in underground passageways.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Over the tannoy came news of steady stream of delays.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Everyone knows the coming months could be among the most difficult yet.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: With winter not far off, Ukrzaliznytsia is already figuring out how to deal with evacuations when the outside temperature can reach -20C or below and snow is lying heavy on the ground.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: Along with international donors, the company is preparing winter evacuation packs, mobile shelters and bus services in areas where evacuations become too frequent.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "We might be a slightly different railway, a reinvented railway," Pertsovskyi said.
sentences.article_title: Fear and disruption for Ukraine's rail passengers as Russia escalates drone attacks

sentences.text: "But we'll keep connecting the country, no matter what, be it winter, be it summer, no matter how hard the enemy hits us." Extra reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko

sentences.text: There are four weeks to go until the US midterm elections, when voters take part in a ballot that could have a major impact on the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: On 3 November, Americans will choose members of Congress, which is made up of two parts - the House of Representatives and the Senate.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Elections take place every two years, and when they happen in the middle of the president's four-year term of office, they are called the midterms.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: A key task of Congress is to create and pass federal laws - laws that apply nationwide.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The outcome of the midterms will decide which political party - Trump's Republicans or opposition Democrats - controls Congress and how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The results are also seen as a measure of how happy people in the US are with the president's performance so far.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: All 435 members of the House - the lower chamber of Congress - will be elected.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: They serve fixed terms of two years.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The House is commonly where proposed laws are introduced and debated.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Meanwhile, 35 of 100 seats in the Senate, the upper chamber, will also be up for grabs.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Senators serve six-year terms.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Among other jobs, they approve or block proposed laws that have been received from the House.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: On the same day, voters across much of the US will also choose state-level politicians.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Governor contests in California, Florida, Georgia and Michigan will be among the most closely watched.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The US economy is on the minds of many voters struggling with the price of fuel, groceries, housing and healthcare.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Inflation remains above the level targeted by the US Federal Reserve, partly down to the war that the US and Israel started with Iran in February.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Democrats argue Trump's programme of trade tariffs has also pushed up prices for Americans.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Immigration is another key issue.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Republicans say Trump has delivered on a major campaign pledge in 2024 by tightening the border and launching a widespread - and often controversial - crackdown on illegal immigration.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Concerns over AI have grown in urgency in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Senior politicians from both parties have agreed on the need to regulate it - setting themselves in opposition to Trump, who has rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Congress is one of the three branches of government, alongside the presidency and the judiciary.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Control of it matters for the shaping of legislation.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Both the House and Senate are currently held by the Republican Party.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: But its majority is a slender one.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: They have 218 seats in the House, which is the minimum number needed to control it, plus one independent who votes with them.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: In the Senate, they have 53 seats.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The upper chamber will only change hands if the Democrats win 51 seats, which would overcome a tie-breaking vote by the vice-president - currently a Republican - in the event of both sides getting 50.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: If opposition Democrats win back control of at least one chamber, they will gain power to bring their own laws to the floor.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Voters have tended to "punish" the party of the president in the past and vote against them.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Recent polling shows a low approval rating for the president.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: He began his second term as president with an approval rating of just over 50%, according to polling resource website Silver Bulletin, but in early October it was sitting at about 37%.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Meanwhile 61% disapproved of him.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: But not all seats in each chamber are competitive.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Some are a safe bet for Republicans or Democrats.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The BBC's US partner CBS News has identified nine Senate races to watch , external , in states like Iowa and New Hampshire, and 42 House races, in states like Arizona and Ohio.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The vote is more unpredictable this year because of a battle between the two parties over the way voting districts in the House of Representatives are drawn.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Republicans tried to gain an advantage by creating more favourable electoral maps in certain states and Democrats followed suit.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Josh Turek (Democrat) and Ashley Hinson (Republican) are in a tight race for Iowa's Senate seat If the Democrats win either the House or the Senate then Trump will find it difficult to get any laws through Congress.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: So his domestic plans could be frustrated, although he has found ways to exercise power without his wider party.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Democratic control of either chamber would also mean they could use committees to investigate aspects of the Trump presidency.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Corruption allegations, the new White House ballroom and ICE tactics could be subject to scrutiny.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: There is also a debate within the Democratic Party about whether to impeach Trump, which means to bring charges in Congress that will form the basis for a political, not criminal, trial.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: If the Republican Party stays in control of Congress, Trump will be able to keep going with his plans for the remainder of his time in office.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: The president's name is not on the ballot during the midterm elections, though Trump has urged Republicans to pretend that it is by voting for him as an endorsement of his actions so far.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Whichever way the results fall, commentators are likely to use them to make arguments about how voters feel about the direction of the country under Trump's leadership.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: Trump cannot run to be president a third time.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: After the midterms, we can expect speculation to start building about who might be his successor as the Republican presidential nominee for 2028 - and who might compete against that person for the Democrats.
sentences.article_title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls Every morning at 6am, 10-year-old Rafeef and her younger brother get ready for school, putting on their cream and brown uniforms.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: She always looks forward to seeing her friends and learning about everything from maths to Arabic and Islamic studies.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: She can't wait to start studying English next year.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: But for Rafeef, the journey to school involves far greater risks than crossing roads or missing the bus.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Her school in Taiz, south-western Yemen, stands on a mountain at the edge of a valley known as no-man's land - a heavily contested front line in the civil war between forces supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia, and the Iran-backed Houthis.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: On one side of the school is government-held territory, on the other are Houthi sniper positions.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Rafeef's home is further down the mountain.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Every time she goes to school, she has to walk uphill with her back towards the snipers.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Rafeef's school is overlooked by Houthi positions on the mountains beyond the valley According to Unicef, roughly 3.2 million children in Yemen were out of school even before the war escalated last month.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: It says thousands of children have been killed or maimed since the war began in 2014, while thousands more have been recruited by armed groups on both sides.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Yet despite the risks, Rafeef says she does not want to stop going because she loves seeing her friends and it is her only chance to be with them.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: She begins naming the children in her classroom.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Going to school is the only time Rafeef's parents let her go outside.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: They say they are keen for her to get an education and have the chance of a better life.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Rafeef hopes to become a doctor.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Rafeef's family moved to Taiz from the coastal city of Hudaydah nine years ago, seeking safety when Houthis took control there.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: But Taiz has also endured fighting.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Rafeef says that two years ago there was a mortar attack outside her new home.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: "Everyone was out except for me and my brother.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Then a mortar came out of nowhere… shrapnel blew through the door and into the house." Her arm was broken and there is still a scar where she was hit.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: And in recent days the conflict has intensified.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: On Sunday the Houthis cut off a vital supply route linking Taiz to Aden, which meant they were able to effectively encircle Taiz.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Control of that route has kept shifting.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Residents have told the BBC they are afraid the Houthis could seize the city at any moment.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Government forces have made gains in other areas this week, they say, retaking control of strategic points on the Bab al-Mandab Strait - a key shipping chokepoint - and launching an offensive to try to regain control of the capital, Sanaa.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway Homes in Taiz are mostly scattered across the slopes, but many have been abandoned by families fleeing the fighting.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Twice, we try to visit the neighbourhood where Rafeef and her family live, but a community leader advises us it is too dangerous.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: On the first occasion, residents of the neighbourhood tell us that three people have been shot by snipers.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: On the second, we are told of another shooting.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: At Rafeef's school, one of the teachers, Abdel Raqeeb al-Obaidi, 45, takes us on to the rooftop to show us what he says are Houthi military camps, barracks and sniper positions in the mountains.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Standing on the rooftop, a Yemeni security adviser accompanying us suddenly tells us to go back inside.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: We are visible from these positions and could be shot, he says.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Abdel Raqeeb laughs, acknowledging the danger.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: He says the school has been fired on before.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: "The situation may explode at any moment while we are sitting in class or sleeping or we are in school or we are out on the street.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: We do not know how our future is and how tomorrow is." For Abdel Raqeeb, the risk has become routine.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: His familiarity with it is unsettling.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Taiz has long been a major battleground in the country's devastating civil war.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: After ousting the government from the capital Sanaa in 2015, the Houthis attempted to also seize control of Taiz but were driven out of most of the city by local militiamen.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Seizing Taiz would give the Houthis full control over the country's north.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Now, in their latest offensive, Houthis are making extensive use of drones alongside other weapons.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Sometimes civilians are collateral damage in the fighting.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Later that evening, we get a call from a hospital about a five minute drive away from the school.
sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Two children have been badly injured by a mortar strike.

sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.article_title: Children brave snipers and mortars to go to school near Yemen front line

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Defence secretary Pete Hegseth has publicly criticised Anthropic's boss Dario Amodei The US Department of Defence is no longer using Anthropic's AI tools, an official has told the BBC, months after it designated the company a supply chain risk on national security grounds.

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.

sentences.text: Overcoming social anxiety can be tricky but experts have shared some tips to try and make it easier It was during her teenage years that Mary began to become anxious in social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It got so bad she developed depression and had to have time off school.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: By the time she started university, she avoided group settings altogether.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I didn't join clubs and societies like others did," says Mary (not her real name).
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I just thought nobody would want to get to know me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I didn't really make a single friend during my whole degree." Mary's social anxiety was so bad that she was diagnosed as having social anxiety disorder - something that affects up to 12% of people , external at some point in their lives.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: But plenty more report struggling more generally.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: As students return to uni, we asked experts how to overcome these feelings whether in your first, or final year.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: This video can not be played What makes you socially anxious?
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Research has suggested more than a fifth of university students face some kind of social anxiety during their studies – and it has been linked to lower grades, poorer relationships and isolation in a study by the universities of Chichester, Coventry and University College London , external .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For many, university marks the first time they have moved out of home – and the expectation is that they will quickly make friends.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who went to the University of Exeter, says she did try.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I first got there I went to one society, but everybody was talking to each other and I had a sudden fear come over me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I felt I wouldn't fit in and I went home." Mary, who is now 25, describes her social anxiety as like an out of body experience.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: When she was talking to new people, heat would rise in her face and her hands would begin to tingle.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'd almost feel myself separating from my body.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I forgot how to form words," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "After social situations I was often left with the sense that I'd done something awful.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I had an all-consuming feel of shame.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I kept thinking there was something fundamentally flawed in me." Neil Greening, chair of the Social Anxiety Alliance UK, says this is a typical characteristic of people with social anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People think they have a personality flaw.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: They internalise it rather than seeing it as a recognisable condition that they can get help for." The key thing to remember: It's fairly normal to feel a little shy or anxious when meeting new people, being in new situations or going for a job interview.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Social anxiety is when it actually stops people doing things, Greening says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For those with a clinical diagnosis it can have a debilitating impact like it did for Mary.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It can be hard to admit to any form of social anxiety in a world where extrovertism and social confidence is generally admired.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who has moved on to do a postgraduate course, is now managing her social anxiety better.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: After her undergraduate degree she got support from the NHS in the form of a talking therapy called CBT.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It is considered the gold standard treatment for social anxiety and encourages people to re-frame their thoughts and change their behaviours.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Prof David Clark, a psychologist at the University of Oxford, says he would like to see more people come forward for therapy but says people can also take steps to help themselves.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The first step, he says, is to stop obsessive self-focus .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often monitor themselves constantly during social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "Focus outwardly on the conversation, other person or your surroundings." He says you also need to test your fears with behavioural experiments by asking a question in a meeting or saying something in a group and noticing what happens.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often assume negative outcomes – that they will embarrass themselves or think others will find them boring.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Testing that can help people break that.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's frightening, but it can really help." He also says they need to drop safety behaviours , such as rehearsing every sentence, avoiding eye contact or sticking close to one particular person.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: And finally, Clark adds, try to avoid post-event rumination .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It's so easy to distort what actually happened." This is something Mary can empathise with.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I used to play things over constantly in my mind.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: What I've learnt is that dealing with social anxiety is a gradual process.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The therapy really helped me, but so did something a friend said to me a couple of years ago.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I said I didn't want to join her in meeting some of her friends, citing my poor social skills, she said she'd never thought that about me and that I shouldn't undersell myself.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I was overcome with emotion.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'm now pushing myself to engage more.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It helps that in my postgrad course we're in smaller groups, but I've also joined an astronomy group.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's still difficult and it doesn't always go how I want it to, but I'm learning to manage it." Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse Why caffeine makes some people buzz - and others barely notice
