sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Louise died about a month after receiving her cancer diagnosis The family of a 24-year-old woman who died after her smear test was said to have been misread has supported calls for a public inquiry into Northern Ireland's cervical screening service.

sentences.text: Louise Corbett Gibbons, from near Katesbridge in County Down, died from cervical cancer in 2008.
sentences.article_title: Family of woman who died after 'misread' smear test join calls for inquiry

sentences.text: Her death is not linked to the cervical screening scandal involving the Southern Health Trust but her widower Neville Gibbons and aunt Joy Fairley joined campaigners to mark three years since those issues came to light.
sentences.article_title: Family of woman who died after 'misread' smear test join calls for inquiry

sentences.text: The Southern Trust scandal led to 17,500 women being approached to have their smear tests rechecked as part of a major review of screening dating back to 2008.
sentences.article_title: Family of woman who died after 'misread' smear test join calls for inquiry

sentences.text: Louise's loved ones are supporting calls for an inquiry into cervical screening services Campaigners calling themselves the Ladies with Letters have since been calling for a statutory public inquiry into what went wrong.

sentences.text: He said the pair, who had been together for eight years, got married the following week.

sentences.article_title: Family of woman who died after 'misread' smear test join calls for inquiry

sentences.text: Sally Williams told the BBC how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause For three years, Sally Williams struggled to understand what was happening to her as her mental health deteriorated and her life fell apart, spending almost 11 months in hospital across eight admissions.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: She left her finance job, was separated from her teenage son and found herself fighting for her life, unaware her symptoms could be linked to perimenopause.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "No one joined the dots," Williams said.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I joined the dots and it was transformational to start hormone replacement therapy and literally come back to life." Williams, who initially self-diagnosed, wants other women to be aware of perimenopause, the years leading up to menopause, which she described as the "danger zone".
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Perimenopause , external , which commonly begins around the age of 46, is when women experience menopause symptoms while still having periods.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Symptoms can include anxiety, mood swings, brain fog, hot flushes and irregular periods, with some women taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to help  alleviate the symptoms.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: What is the menopause and what are the main signs?
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: How does Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) work?
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: When her symptoms began in her late 40s, Williams, from the Wychavon area, said doctors she saw initially thought she had depression.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "I had multiple attempts on my life, two significant ones, one where I was in a wheelchair for three months for polytrauma, and this was in Covid, so there were no visitors.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I had no contact with anyone," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: This was at perimenopause time.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: My message to women is that, menopause is not the danger zone, it's the run up, it's the 45 to 54." For Williams, who said she was "unrecognisable" before her eventual diagnosis, it was HRT which eventually helped her, but she said it may not be for everyone.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: The drug , which isn't suitable for some women, tops up and stabilises oestrogen levels, sometimes in combination with a synthetic or bioidentical version of progesterone.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Williams is set to speak about her hard fought menopause diagnosis at Meno Fest at Worcester Rugby Club on 7 October , external , as part of Menopause Awareness Month.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: The free event is being held with the aim of helping people to gain greater understanding of how perimenopause and menopause can affect every aspect of life from physical and mental health to relationships, work and family life.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Williams told the BBC of how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I didn't see my friends, my family for three years and I was a recluse.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: And my son, who was in his teens, I probably saw him three times," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "He had leave his school and his friends and he had to go and live with his dad because he couldn't see me.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I couldn't care for him." It was also important that men recognised what was happening to women during perimenopause, she added.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "I think men need to come into the conversation as well, and I'm not just talking husbands and partners, I'm talking sons," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "It was devastating and there's relationships that have been broken that will never be put back together.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Dr Amara Naseem says GPs are under pressure to offer more appointments, rather than a focus on quality treatment Pressure to provide more GP appointments is making it harder to include checks for gynaecological cancers within the 10-minute slots, doctors have said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Dr Amara Naseem says her clinics always overrun as it takes about 20 minutes to sensitively take a detailed history and carry out internal examinations.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: A reduced number of practices in her area means she has taken on more patients and fears there is a risk that women will not raise gynaecological symptoms or attend screenings if appointments are rushed, painful or not handled well.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it was increasing investment in primary care and recruiting up to 100 extra GPs.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Research by cancer charity Tenovus, in support of Claire's Campaign , external , found about half of the 100 GPs surveyed across Wales felt limited consultation time was a major concern.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: A third also had concerns about "over-referring" people for further testing to rule out cancers, given hospitals are already overstretched.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Currently, 95% of patients put on the suspected cancer pathway are later told they do not have cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: But doctors said teasing out the cancer cases at an early stage could be challenging when symptoms such as bloating are hard to distinguish from benign conditions including irritable bowel syndrome.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Naseem said the pressure from the Welsh government was to "offer more appointments to the patient, rather than about the quality of the treatment".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Lowri Griffiths of Tenovus said incidence and mortality rates for gynaecological cancers in Wales were higher than the UK average - something she added the Welsh government needed "to get to grips with".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Pledges to increase GP numbers were promising, she said, "but unless we address both the primary care setting and the hospital setting, the system won't work".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Lowri Griffiths says Wales needs to be "more aspirational" in gynaecological care Naseem said many women's health issues may require an internal examination, which requires time to be done "in an empathetic and sensitive way".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She added: "I'm working in a very diverse community, also in a deprived community, where uptake of screening is already low." She said in communities where myths existed around screening, time is also required to explain what is involved and allay fears and potentially work with interpreters.

sentences.text: Dr Kathrin Thomas said her friend Claire O'Shea was "a real feminist" Dr Kathrin Thomas, a former GP and public health specialist, got involved in Claire's Campaign when her friend Claire O'Shea was given a late diagnosis for a gynaecological cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Claire, from Cardiff, died last year, aged 42.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Thomas said GP numbers in Wales had "almost flat-lined" while the workload had increased, especially in more disadvantaged areas where there were "fewer doctors, fewer nurses and the healthcare needs are much greater".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She is also involved with Deep End Cymru - a network of GP practices in the most deprived areas.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "We've got a big difference in the cancer experience in more deprived communities - cervical cancer in particular," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "There's a wide inequity between women in more affluent areas and women in poorer areas." Of the 1,200 women diagnosed, about 470 patients die from a gynaecological cancer, either of the womb (uterine), ovary, cervix, vulva or vagina, in Wales each year.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Charlotte McCann said the trial gave her hope for the future Charlotte McCann has been dealing with severe pain from endometriosis since she was 14.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: It became so intolerable as an adult she had to leave her chosen career.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: She would wake up in the night vomiting, and on some days Charlotte found she could not stand or get out of bed.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: It is a myth that endometriosis is a painful period condition - rather, it is a system-wide inflammatory disease where cells, similar to those which line the womb, start to grow in other parts of the body.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: This can be on the bowel or in the lungs - and the cells multiply, creating raw and angry sores.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Those affected can wait years for diagnosis, and there is no cure - meaning women are left grappling with debilitating pain that can affect their relationships, work, education and mental health.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Now aged 27, Charlotte hopes a new pain management programme for the condition, which is being trialled as part of a £2.3m study, might help others in her position.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: The UK-wide study, led by the University of Aberdeen and NHS Grampian, will include pain medication alongside other treatments such as physiotherapy, and will investigate whether a personalised plan can improve quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: This video can not be played Hope for new endometriosis trial in Aberdeen Charlotte, from Huntly in Aberdeenshire, is currently living with stage 4 endometriosis , external .
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: She had to abandon her career in corporate finance due to the pain, and now works as a freelance pet-sitter when she can.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "I would wake up in the night vomiting and I was always worried that maybe my appendix had burst or I had a kidney infection or something like that," she recalled.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "The pain would come on so strong, I wouldn't be able to even sit up straight, I wouldn't be able to stand up.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "It was heavily disrupting my life.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: I couldn't focus on anything, and I couldn't sleep or eat because of the pain.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "There's no way I could continue my nine-to-five job when I could barely sit up." Charlotte said she had years of not knowing what was wrong, until an MRI scan confirmed endometriosis.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Women can wait years for an endometriosis diagnosis.

sentences.text: "I am now on very strong opioid painkillers to try to get on top of the pain, but they make me feel very sick, to the point I can't eat, so I have lost a lot of weight now as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Charlotte described being in so much pain that there are days when she cannot get out of bed.

sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Once participants are recruited, they will take part in a 12-week personalised programme - called an endometriosis-specific pain management programme (e-PMP).
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: The project will evaluate whether this strategy can offer more effective treatment for women who find their pain is not adequately controlled by surgery or medication.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: It includes cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)-informed psychotherapy, specialist physiotherapy, guidance on relationships, intimacy and communication, and medication to reduce side effects.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds Pre-menopausal women will either receive the new programme alongside existing standard care, or existing standard care alone, with the results of each approach then compared.

sentences.text: Eligible participants will be recruited to the study by their specialist.

sentences.text: Consultant gynaecologist Dr Lucky Saraswat, an honorary senior lecturer at the university, and lead for Aberdeen Endometriosis Centre at NHS Grampian, is heading the study.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Dr Lucky Saraswat is leading the new study "Endometriosis is one of the most common yet under researched causes of chronic pain," she said.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "Many women continue to suffer even after surgery or medication.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "This study will help us understand whether a tailored, interdisciplinary pain management programme can offer meaningful, long term improvements in quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "If effective, e-PMP could become a vital new treatment option, particularly for women who wish to avoid repeated surgery or hormonal therapies, or who are planning a pregnancy." Alongside the clinical results, the study will also aim to assess cost effectiveness.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: Prof Anthony Gordon, director of NIHR's health technology assessment programme, said many women could face years of "agonising" symptoms with few long-term options.
sentences.article_title: Endometriosis trial gives hope to millions of women in pain like me

sentences.text: "High-quality research is essential to break this cycle and deliver treatment that addresses the full, complex impact of endometriosis," he said.

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: York was the subject of the city-wide pilot, which also put on workshops for parents and offered special training for early years staff.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England are now signed up to launch similar schemes to tackle the number of pupils starting school without being fully toilet-trained.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government said the pilot's results were "encouraging", and confirmed they were committed to 75% of pupils reaching a good level of development at the end of their first year in school by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Since April this year, parents across York have been targeted via GP surgeries, pharmacies, family hubs, schools, nurseries and libraries with information and offers of support on how to potty-train their child ahead of starting school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Potty training guides were sent out to all families across York who had a child starting reception in September - with the aim that all children could use the toilet independently by the time they started school, except those with medical issues or special educational needs.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The results from all 55 mainstream primary schools across the city, shared exclusively with BBC News, suggested there had been a 43% drop since last year in the number of children who were not fully toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Across York last September, 148 out of 1,364 reception pupils (11%) were recorded as not being toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: This year, that fell to 85 reception pupils out of 1,374 (6%).
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Parents Natalie and Lucy, who both have daughters starting reception next year, have welcomed the extra support on offer.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Mum Natalie says there's a lot of conflicting pressures on parents about the right time to potty-train Lucy said she had noticed the drop-in sessions on potty training in her local children's centre and thought it was a "really good idea".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think it's really important that children are more prepared for that aspect of starting school," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Natalie said getting her daughter Freya potty-trained in time for school has been a priority, but feels there is a lot of pressure on parents to do so.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think going to school is hard enough for children," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When I was little, we still had the terry towelling nappies and they had to be washed and hung on the line.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So I think with disposable nappies it's easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: When parenting advice becomes too much Before Rosie Whitfield became a mum, she imagined herself parenting very calm children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Then I had two wild boys," she says with a laugh.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Following the birth of her kids, Rosie spent hours online looking for the best advice and was drawn to one particular approach to parenting: Gentle parenting, which focuses on empathy and mutual respect with little emphasis on punishment, albeit with boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But she constantly worried her choices, from sleep schedules to handling toddler tantrums, were "ruining their lives forever".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie believes her confidence and intuition were stripped away as she questioned every parenting decision.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Government research suggests that around two-thirds of parents with young children feel overwhelmed by the amount of parenting information available and struggle with conflicting advice, with many turning to social media for support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie Whitfield says she felt overwhelmed by the amount of parenting advice online when looking for guidance on raising her two sons.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And it's not just the early years.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research from the charity Action for Children found that many parents of teenagers who initially contacted the charity for help with school avoidance, ADHD or mental health, often went on to describe their own anxiety, exhaustion and uncertainty of how to parent with empathy and patience when close to burnout.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Faced with an array of parenting philosophies, or "brands" to choose from, is all of this advice helping parents or making them more anxious?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And is there really a best way to parent?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Or, as we strive to become the perfect parent, are we losing our intuition?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents today are confronted by parenting styles including "helicopter parenting", which is focused on closely monitoring and protecting children from harm, and "tiger parenting", which involves strict parenting and high expectations for achievement.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also "snowplough parents", who try to remove obstacles from their child's path, and "dolphin parents", who aim to be firm but flexible.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Author Matilda Gosling, who wrote Evidence‑Based Parenting, says many of the parenting fads or trends complicate what should be a straightforward relationship between a parent and child.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Throughout history, you get these swings from one extreme to the other," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gentle parenting is seen by some as the latest swing away from a strict, detached parenting style popular in the 1990s, which often relied on controlled crying, the naughty step and time out.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It is built around understanding, empathy and respect but also emphasises the importance of boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: One of the most widely studied models of parenting comes from developmental psychologist Diana Baumrind.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Baumrind identified three parenting styles, later expanded to four: authoritative (high warmth and high control), authoritarian (low warmth and high control), permissive (high warmth and low control), and neglectful (low warmth and low control).
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Authoritative is the gold standard," says Gosling who has looked at more than 1,000 studies.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research has found that children raised with an authoritative approach, combining warmth with clear boundaries, tend to achieve better academic results, have higher self-esteem and stronger social skills.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But where gentle parenting fits within that framework is disputed.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gosling believes that it falls on the permissive side.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's very much child-led.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The child ends up having so much control that there's no sense of safety coming from the outside." However, Sarah Ockwell-Smith, who is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting', strongly disagrees.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It [gentle parenting] is not remotely permissive," she says, putting it firmly in Baumrind's authoritative category.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Clear boundaries are "super important".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Social media, however, is flooded with memes of exhausted parents calmly negotiating with a child having a supermarket meltdown, something Ockwell-Smith finds deeply frustrating.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I have to step away from the Instagram reels and the TikToks because I just want to comment, 'This is not gentle parenting'".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "You have house rules, family limits, discipline and consequences.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But the difference is we look at discipline as learning and teaching rather than punishing." Toddler tantrums and teenage behaviour, she argues, should be viewed through a lens of ongoing brain development, not 'they're being naughty' or 'they hate me'.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But despite the term being popular, Ockwell-Smith believes that gentle parenting is still a fringe movement and that authoritarian parenting remains the dominant style.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Around 80 years ago, American paediatrician Dr Benjamin Spock published a book called Baby and Child Care, which went on to sell millions of copies and became the main source of advice for mothers for generations.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The opening line was "Trust yourself.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: You know more than you think..." The book challenged strict parenting norms of the time and in the following decades parents were offered more advice from an increasing range of voices.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research into parenting has increasingly focused on the early years - from pregnancy to the age of two when the building blocks for lifelong emotional and physical health are laid down.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: For parents, that means more advice to navigate competing messages about what is best for their children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Professor Ellie Lee, the director of the Centre for Parenting Culture Studies, has studied parenting for more than two decades, including research into mothers' confidence and uncertainty around infant feeding.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She says a major shift occurred in the 1990s when parenting became an increasing focus of public policy.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Politicians started to say 'Parenting's the hardest job in the world.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Children don't come with a manual.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: We need to give parents guidance.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents need more support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: We need parent education'." Advice began to emerge on almost every aspect of family life, from tummy time, to feeding, to the right buggy, she explains.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Prof Lee argues that while some public health campaigns were necessary, such as advice not to put babies to sleep on their front after research into cot deaths, the growing culture of advice began to make parents paranoid.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Dr Spock's 'trust yourself' philosophy is now a very counter-cultural piece of advice," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "What we say instead is 'always seek help'," Sarah Ockwell-Smith is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting' She believes this has made parents more anxious about doing things "right".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Some of the things that are now presented as really high stakes are not," she says, using examples like breastfeeding exclusively for six months or how much tummy time a child needs.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's terrible because parents become completely exhausted." Ockwell-Smith says the volume of advice can be "deafening and confusing".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Actually, parents should just learn themselves and go on intuition," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Others point out that there is also a problem of advice being given that is altogether wrong.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Ruth Watts is a health visitor who began sharing content on social media after becoming concerned about misinformation online.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She had seen "experts" advise parents to wean babies onto solids early, offer treatment advice for tongue tie or allergies without medical training, and tell parents to put babies in their own rooms before six months.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Many families, she argues, are working longer hours while at the same time health services are being stripped back, leaving more parents looking online for breastfeeding, behaviour and sleep support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "We are looking for that kind of personable, conversational approach from people, rather than reading a website." Many factors shaping family life remain outside parents' control.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: A child's temperament, special educational needs, family support, finances and their own upbringing can all influence family life.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: While some say parenting hasn't got harder but expectations have, others argue that parents today are facing more complex challenges than in previous generations with growing concerns around young people's mental health.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also debates around children spending more time on screens and less time outdoors, while schools are reporting increasing behavioural challenges and lower respect for rules and authority.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Prof Lee believes parental confidence is at an all-time low.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I think parents feel very nervous about disciplining children now because they're worried about how it's going to make them feel," she argues.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The confusion around the "right" way to parent has led some parents to turn to courses for help.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Aymara Lamche-Brennan, who has a 22-year-old daughter, four-year-old son and six-month-old daughter, signed up for a course during the summer when another mother at the school gate mentioned she was attending.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Aymara Lamche-Brennan, pictured with her three children, signed up for a Circle of Security parenting course "The flyer said 'it's the toughest job in the world' and I thought yes it is, how can you help?'" Aymara says from her home in London.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's not telling you how to parent.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It's helping you think," says Jennifer Peters, a former social worker and director of the charity Connected Lives which runs courses across London, Derbyshire and Cambridgeshire.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: She says most parents want the best for their kids but they don't always know how to get there, and that guidance can be helpful.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I don't think people need to be bombarded with information but the group experience helps you think, 'oh, it's not just me' and lets you take a step back from it all," Peters says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Back in Dubai, Rosie says the arrival of her second child changed everything as she realised her sons were "polar opposites" and there is no one-size-fits-all solution.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: A recent trip home to Birmingham also provided some perspective.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Her eldest son was throwing a tantrum, and Rosie found herself wrestling with a familiar worry.

sentences.text: "If I send him upstairs, am I damaging him emotionally?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Is he going to develop an attachment disorder because of this?" But her mum said, 'Just send him upstairs.

sentences.text: He can't hit his brother over the head with a horse [if he is upstairs].

sentences.text: Big moments from Olivia Rodrigo's tour were dissected online shortly after her opening night Months before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.

sentences.article_title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?

sentences.article_title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?

sentences.text: The photo, taken in 1978, has been exhibited around the world When Vivienne Dawes first saw the photograph of herself dancing on a crowded dance floor almost 50 years ago, it felt like being transported back in time.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Captured at Wolverhampton's Culture Centre in 1978, the image shows her among a group of young people immersed in a night of music and dancing.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: At the time, none of them could have known the photograph would become an iconic image that has been viewed across the world and one of photographer Chris Steele-Perkins' most recognised works.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Nor could they have imagined that, decades later, they would be reunited through the photo and finally have their stories told.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "Oh my goodness - oh my, and I do look like me, don't I?" Vivianne said when she saw the image.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: She is the central dancer in the photograph and can still remember the atmosphere inside the venue.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: She said: "Back then, everybody was doing their own thing, was all dancing, and when the music hit us, we felt no pain.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Now it is going on display in its home city of Wolverhampton, at the Grand theatre.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Vivienne said she had no awareness when she was dancing that her photo was being taken.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "If you notice the way we all dance, it's like we were on another planet," she said.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Her dance, as captured in the photo, would also later go on to be recreated in a painting by artist Claudette Johnson , external , which will also appear in the Wolverhampton exhibition.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "It's beautiful," Vivienne said.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "I appreciated the fact that someone could put their time into painting a portrait of me.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "I can't believe I looked so attractive back then, really and truly.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: I look very lovely." While the photo has become celebrated over the years, the people captured in it have remained largely anonymous, until now.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: For Winston Logan, who appears at the back of the photo on the far left, the image is a reminder of a very different Wolverhampton.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Having arrived in Britain about five years before the photo was taken, he remembers a lack of opportunities for young Black people.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "Life is hard, no entertainment, nowhere to go, no fun," he said.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: But the Culture Centre on Clarence Street offered something different, becoming a hub for music, dancing and community.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: Looking back, Winston sees the image as a snapshot of a pivotal period in his life.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "This is where it starts, [I] went from unemployment, went from there into training, went from there into industry, construction or whatever, and now I'm passing on my skills.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "Mum and dad didn't get to see that photo or find out about that photo." "This time, to the present day, my life has, I would say, blown up.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: He described it as a difficult commission, adding that he had not really liked the photo at the time, although it had grown on him since and had become his best-selling print.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: "You can hear it, you can smell it, you can feel that image.
sentences.article_title: Dancers reunited 50 years after disco photo

sentences.text: The Feeling frontman Dan Gillespie Sells said celebrating the 20th anniversary of their breakthrough album was "extraordinary" The Feeling's triple-platinum debut album was recorded in a shed in Horsham, according to frontman Dan Gillespie Sells.
sentences.article_title: The Feeling album recorded in a Sussex shed

sentences.text: I think about what a different world it was then.

sentences.text: Lionel Messi will earn his 208th cap for Argentina in the friendly against Benin Twenty-one years after Lionel Messi helped Argentina beat Nigeria in the Under-20 World Cup final, another African side will be on the pitch for the final match of his international career.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: Benin face Argentina at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday in a farewell match for the 39-year-old.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: For Benin assistant coach Tunde Adelakun, there is a neat symmetry to the occasion.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "Africa has been at the heart of Messi's remarkable career," he told BBC Sport Africa.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "I was physically there when they beat Nigeria in the final, where he was the most valuable player in that tournament.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "It's an absolute pleasure that, when he is drawing the curtain on his international career, Benin will be part of that." Messi announced his international retirement on 31 August after Argentina's defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: Argentina's most-capped player and record goalscorer has scored 125 times in 207 senior internationals.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "Everybody was absolutely ecstatic," Adelakun says.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: Head coach Gernot Rohr says his side will enjoy "a bit of a party with Messi", but has stressed that they are not travelling to Buenos Aires simply to make up the numbers.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: In his six World Cup appearances, Messi played against five African countries, including three, (Algeria, Cape Verde and Egypt) at the 2026 tournament in North America.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: There is history behind the African connection to Messi's international career.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: Di Maria scored the only goal as Nigeria took silver.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: For Adelakun, Messi's longevity and mentality are as significant as the trophies and goals.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "He is the very best of them all," he says.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: But Mounié is not expecting Benin's players to spend the final whistle fighting over one famous souvenir.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: Asked whether they will chase Messi's shirt, the captain says the moment should belong to the Argentine.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "If I was him, I wouldn't give my jersey to anyone, to be honest," he says.
sentences.article_title: Benin prepare for 'historic' role in Messi's Argentina farewell

sentences.text: "He needs to enjoy this moment as a football player, and he deserves to have a moment where he just enjoys."
